take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only when the agents need different access, a different dialect or a different stance. 'Three is more thorough' is not a reason.
A synthesizer given no framework just averages the views. If I give it a framework such as diagnosis, policy and actions, it has to pick one. I can use that for a leadership-team question.

Mistakes happen at the handoffs, and nothing here checks whether the final briefing is true. A person still has to, and an agent's access to employee data is a question for the works council and the DPO.

monday.move: Ask my team who would own an agent for the weekly people-metrics summary. Then ask the DPO and the works council what an agent may access and whether it may only propose actions.
monday.who: Me, one HR partner, the DPO
monday.when: Monday, a 30-minute chat before I build anything
monday.stop_condition: If employee data cannot go into the tool, I build nothing and write down what we need to decide.
monday.blocker: I haven't asked the works council or the DPO about employee data in an AI tool.

misconception.why: The module never touched headcount or roles. The access point (legal-policy agent without customer data) and the 'who owns it' question made me more careful, but I still believe agents replace headcount first.

one_line: Useful rule of thumb: don't split into several agents unless you need different access, language or opinions. But it's a tooling day, and it never said what any of this means for my people.
